subsections.title: What the company actually does, in plain terms

blocks.text: ABB India Limited manufactures and sells electrification, motion and process-automation hardware, systems and services to Indian industry, infrastructure and, increasingly, data centres. [F] (SCREENER) It was incorporated in 1949 and has been manufacturing in India for more than 75 years. [F] (AR2025 p.25) It operates five manufacturing locations - Bengaluru (Peenya and Nelamangala), Faridabad, Nashik and Vadodara - housing 25 plants, with 28 sales offices, 750-plus channel partners and exports to over 30 countries. [F] (AR2025 p.21) A sixth manufacturing location was added at Nelamangala in the first half of CY2026. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) Permanent headcount was 3,859 at December 2025 against 3,625 a year earlier; total people on site including offices and shop floors were about 5,027. [F] (AR2025 p.27, p.21)

**The fiscal-year convention matters for everything that follows.** ABB India reports on a calendar year ending 31 December, not the Indian April-March year. [F] (AR2025 p.288) In this report CY2025 means January-December 2025; the latest reported quarter is Q2 CY2026 (April-June 2026), which our statements data labels Jun 2026. [F] (NUMBERS) One exchange filing refers to the November 2026 board meeting as covering Q2 FY27 results; that label is inconsistent with the company's own December year-end and with the Q3 CY2026 quarter it will actually report. [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS) [AI] We treat the company's calendar-year basis as authoritative.

Revenue is earned in four reported business segments. For CY2025, segment revenues were Electrification Rs 5,713 crore, Motion Rs 4,561 crore, Process Automation (presented to investors as Automation) Rs 2,332 crore and Robotics and Discrete Automation Rs 701 crore, against a reported consolidated revenue of Rs 13,203 crore after inter-segment eliminations. [F] (AR2025 p.330) That is a mix of roughly 43 / 34 / 18 / 5 percent. [E] The Robotics business has since been carved out: the board approved a slump sale to a fellow ABB entity at not less than Rs 1,568.20 crore in January 2026, and the CY2026 reported numbers exclude it. [F] (AR2025 p.100, p.341)

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the ten strongest reasons not to own it

blocks.text: The price, not the business, is the bear case. At Rs 7,270 the reverse DCF requires about 82% annual sales growth for five years against 11.6% in the base case. [E] (NUMBERS) Nothing in four earnings calls or the annual report supports growth of that order.

items: 1. **Valuation requires arithmetic the company has never produced.** The reverse DCF implies a five-year sales CAGR of 81.7% to justify today's enterprise value, against a base-case equivalent of 10.8%. Bear, base and bull fair values are Rs 452.9, Rs 814.8 and Rs 1,134.6 per share against a price of Rs 7,270. [E] (NUMBERS) The best five-year revenue record on disclosure is 17% CAGR. [F] (CALL Feb 2026)

2. **Margin erosion is now six quarters old and management will not call the bottom.** Quarterly operating margin fell from 20% (Dec 2024) to 19% (Mar 2025), 14% (Jun 2025), 15% (Sep and Dec 2025), 13% (Mar 2026) and 13% (Jun 2026). [F] (NUMBERS) Asked directly whether the worst is behind, the CFO said he was not comfortable committing to mid-teen EBITDA margins and that the priority was to protect current levels. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

3. **The record CY2025 order headline was carried by the segment that has been sold.** Company orders rose 8% to Rs 14,115 crore. [F] (AR2025 p.28) Within that, Robotics orders more than doubled from Rs 534 crore to Rs 1,217 crore on a one-time automotive order, while Electrification orders actually fell from Rs 6,068 crore to Rs 5,878 crore. [F] (AR2025 p.155, p.150; CALL Feb 2026) Robotics was then approved for slump sale out of the listed company. [F] (AR2025 p.100)

4. **A very large share of the economics leaves the company as related-party payments.** Purchases from related parties were 39.46% of total purchases in CY2025, up from 34.22%. [F] (AR2025 p.174) Royalty, technology and trademark fees of Rs 559.8 crore plus IT, group management, legal and other service charges of Rs 828.0 crore totalled Rs 1,387.9 crore - equal to about 62% of consolidated profit before tax of Rs 2,229.9 crore. [E] (AR2025 p.333, p.334, p.288) These charges grew 17.7% year on year while PBT fell 11.3%. [E]

5. **The company is structurally short the rupee.** Foreign exchange used was Rs 6,764.97 crore in CY2025 against foreign exchange earned of Rs 1,568.35 crore - a net outflow of about Rs 5,197 crore, roughly 39% of revenue. [F] (AR2025 p.109) [E] Management confirms imports are around 20% of cost against exports of about 10% of revenue, and cites rupee depreciation as a repeated margin driver. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026; CALL Aug 2026)

6. **There is no scope for supportive promoter buying and the float is thinning on the institutional side.** Promoter holding has been pinned at exactly 75.0% for all twelve quarters disclosed - the regulatory maximum - so any change can only be downward. [F] (NUMBERS) FII holding fell from 12.28% (Sep 2024) to 7.67% (Jun 2026) while DII holding rose from 5.42% to 9.89%. [F] (NUMBERS)

7. **Cash conversion runs persistently below reported profit.** Operating cash flow was 0.68x reported profit over the last three years. [E] (NUMBERS) The cash conversion cycle worsened from 13 days (CY2024) to 21 days (CY2025) and inventory days rose from 96 to 98 as the company deliberately stocked imported material. [F] (NUMBERS; CALL Nov 2025)

8. **Much of the order book is re-tendered rather than contracted.** In the systems business, bidding is on an L1 basis through reverse auction where price increases cannot be passed on. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Long-term contracts are disclosed only for railway traction. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) The backlog is short: management expects at least 40% of the Rs 11,900 crore to convert within two quarters. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

9. **Leadership is changing at the top and the CFO seat is vacant in prospect.** Sanjeev Sharma hands over to T.K. Sridhar as Managing Director from 1 January 2027; the new CFO had not been identified as of the July 2026 call, with the search expected to complete in a couple of months. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) The incoming MD is the outgoing CFO, so the entire finance leadership turns over at once. [AI]

10. **Disclosure stops exactly where an analyst needs it.** No installed capacity, no utilisation percentage, no named customers, no quantified price increases, no order-book maturity schedule, no split of orders into volume and price, no per-megawatt data-centre content, no separate R&D spend. [F] (AR2025 p.109; CALL May 2026; CALL Aug 2026) Management has declined each of these when asked directly. [F] (CALL May 2026; CALL Aug 2026)

blocks.text: Our variant view is that the debate the market is having - cyclical recovery versus structural margin damage - is the wrong debate, because at Rs 7,270 both answers lose. The business is genuinely good: a AAA-rated, debt-free, 22% return-on-equity franchise with a technology feed from a global parent, a service annuity in automation, and an order book at a record. [F] (RATING; NUMBERS; AR2025 p.339) But the value of that franchise is bounded, and our DCF bounds it at Rs 452.9 to Rs 1,134.6 per share across bear to bull. [E] (NUMBERS) The second-order variant point is subtler and more durable: a rising share of the value this franchise creates is contracted away to the parent before it reaches the minority shareholder. Related-party purchases went from 34.22% to 39.46% of total purchases in one year, and royalty plus group service charges rose 17.7% while profit before tax fell 11.3%. [F] (AR2025 p.174, p.333, p.334) [E] The listed entity is increasingly a manufacturing and distribution node inside a group P&L, and the transfer-pricing dial - not the order book - is the variable with the largest unhedgeable effect on minority earnings. That risk is not priced, because it is not discussed on any of the four calls we reviewed. [AI]

subsections.title: What the timeline reveals about how recent the current business really is

blocks.text: The corporate shell is 77 years old but the current portfolio is roughly seven years old. The single largest historical business - Power Grids, covering high-voltage products, transformers and grid integration - was demerged out to Hitachi Energy India with effect from 1 April 2019, and the residual disclosure is now only a customs-licence contingency of Rs 154.08 crore duty value that management says belongs to Hitachi. [F] (AR2025 p.317) Four further businesses - solar, Linxon, Dodge and turbocharging - were carved out by slump sale in earlier years. [F] (AR2025 p.328) Robotics, the fastest-growing segment by orders in CY2025, is being carved out now. [F] (AR2025 p.100, p.155)

**The implication is that historical financial series are not like-for-like and should not be trend-fitted.** Our statements data shows CY2011 revenue of Rs 7,449 crore and a 4.8% operating margin against CY2025 revenue of Rs 13,203 crore at 15.0%. [F] (NUMBERS) That is not one company improving; it is a different, smaller, higher-margin, product-weighted company left behind after the project-heavy businesses were removed. [AI] Any multiple anchored on 'ABB India historically traded at X' inherits the same defect. Management's own five-year framing - revenue CAGR 17%, PBT CAGR 39%, EPS CAGR 33% from CY2020 to CY2025 - starts from a COVID-depressed base and a post-demerger portfolio. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [AI]

sections.title: How the business actually works and where value is captured

items: Step 1 - Technology. Product designs, platforms and IP come from ABB Group's centralised R&D. ABB India pays royalty, technology and trademark fees for access and does not run a separately reported R&D budget: local activity is limited to localisation, adaptation to Indian conditions and cost-down work. [F] (AR2025 p.109; SCREENER)

Step 2 - Sourcing. Roughly 20% of cost is imported, largely from ABB's European feeder factories; related-party purchases were 39.46% of total purchases in CY2025. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026); [F] (AR2025 p.174) The single largest named supplier was ABB Oy, Helsinki at Rs 484.93 cr, followed by ABB Engineering (Shanghai) Rs 431.31 cr, ABB AG Mannheim Rs 382.74 cr and ABB Schweiz Rs 371.52 cr. [F] (AR2025 p.333)

Step 3 - Manufacture and assembly. Five (now six) locations, 25 plants. Products are made to store, made to order, or engineered to order; the engineered-to-order work sits mainly in Motion and Electrification. [F] (AR2025 p.21; CALL Nov 2025)

Step 4 - Certification. Products and sub-components must be tested and certified under the Bureau of Indian Standards Quality Control Orders before use; lab slots are scarce and deadlines keep moving, which forced the company to substitute globally certified imported material to keep delivery commitments. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025)

Step 5 - Route to market. Four channels: EPC contractors 43%, end users 37%, partners/distributors 10%, OEMs 10% of Q1 CY2026 revenue. [F] (PPT May 2026) 981 dealers and distributors, 750-plus channel partners, 28 sales offices. [F] (AR2025 p.173, p.21)

Step 6 - Execution and revenue recognition. Rs 11,119.32 cr of CY2025 revenue was recognised at a point in time and Rs 1,946.20 cr over time, the latter on fixed-price contracts using percentage of completion. [F] (AR2025 p.334)

Step 7 - Service and installed base. Services were 12% of Q1 CY2026 revenue overall and about 30% of Q2 CY2026 Automation revenue; Motion service orders grew 9% in CY2025. [F] (PPT May 2026); [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); [F] (AR2025 p.152)

subsections.title: Where value is captured, and by whom

blocks.text: Value capture sits in three places, and only two of them accrue to minority shareholders. The first is the brand-and-reference position in specification: management states that customers do not compare ABB with lower-priced brands and come to it for reliability, availability and serviceability. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) The second is the installed base and its service tail, strongest in Process Automation where long-term contracts carry forex variation clauses and services are about 30% of revenue, which is precisely why that segment held 16.4% PBIT margin in CY2025 while Electrification fell. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; CALL Aug 2026); [F] (AR2025 p.330) The third is the parent's: royalty and trademark fees of Rs 559.8 cr, IT and group management charges of Rs 828.0 cr, and a further Rs 19.9 cr of share-plan charges, against consolidated PBT of Rs 2,229.9 cr. [F] (AR2025 p.333, p.334, p.288)

Where value is **not** captured is the tendered systems business. Distribution Solutions management states that in system business the company bids L1 through reverse auction and 'sometimes we are not really able to pass on these prices'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) That is the structural reason the flow (product) business and the project business behave so differently on margin, and why the offering mix - 81% products, 12% services, 7% projects at Q1 CY2026 - is more favourable than the segment labels suggest. [F] (PPT May 2026) [AI]

This is an asset-light manufacturer by any conventional test. Property, plant and equipment was Rs 1,083.86 cr against total assets of Rs 13,638.48 cr at December 2025 - under 8%. [F] (AR2025 p.287) Fixed-asset turnover was 11.05x in CY2025 and 11.48x in CY2024, against 6.2x in CY2011-12. [F] (NUMBERS) Capex has run at 1.8% of sales in each of the last two years, Rs 214 cr and Rs 240 cr. [F] (NUMBERS) CRISIL characterises maintenance capex as Rs 200-300 cr a year, comfortably funded from accrual. [F] (RATING)

Outsourcing shows up as subcontracting charges of Rs 429.62 cr (CY2025) versus Rs 341.68 cr (CY2024), and services from third parties of Rs 211.40 cr versus Rs 153.68 cr - both growing faster than revenue. [F] (AR2025 p.288, p.316) [E] Combined with purchases of stock-in-trade of Rs 1,106.78 cr, a meaningful and rising share of what the company sells it does not make. [F] (AR2025 p.288) [AI] The consequence is that the balance sheet is dominated by working capital and cash, not by plant - which is why the return metrics look exceptional and why they are more a function of the payables cycle than of manufacturing efficiency.

blocks.text: **Where ABB sits in the value chain.** Data-centre capital cost splits broadly into compute, building shell, cooling and electrical infrastructure. ABB competes only in the electrical layer, and not all of it. Its disclosed scope is: medium-voltage substations and switchgear bringing power in; medium-voltage primary and secondary distribution; low-voltage switchgear and busway distributing to racks; uninterruptible power supplies and power distribution units; installation products; and components for cooling systems and alternate power sources. [F] (PPT May 2026) The presentation footnotes are explicit about the limits: 'ABB does not offer full scope for cooling and gensets, only components like motors, drives and generators', and alternate power sources other than gensets 'are not yet widespread'. [F] (PPT May 2026)

**What exists today versus narrative.** What exists: orders. Data centres were 10-11% of the December 2025 backlog, 12-13% (range 12-16%) of the March 2026 order book, and 15-17% of Q2 CY2026 order intake - the largest single end-market in that quarter. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026; CALL May 2026; CALL Aug 2026) Named CY2025 wins include low-voltage panels for leading Mumbai data-centre operators, major colocation players in Mumbai and Pune, a global cloud service provider, and unloading/installation/testing/commissioning plus annual maintenance for a leading provider. [F] (AR2025 p.150) A second Nelamangala factory was launched in Q1 CY2026 for new data-centre products, and Distribution Solutions is 'investing quite heavily' in breaker capacity because 'maybe like 2027, 2028, we will be struggling to meet those demand'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**What is narrative.** The per-megawatt scope value. Asked directly for the addressable opportunity per megawatt, the Managing Director said 'yes, we do know what is a factored scope per megawatt, but this is something we don't publicly talk about'. blocks.text: No per-unit economics can be constructed for ABB India from these documents. There is no disclosure of installed capacity, production volume, units sold, tonnage, megawatts shipped, panels delivered, motors produced, or average realisation - in the annual report, the investor presentation, the rating rationale or four earnings calls. [F] (AR2025; PPT May 2026; RATING) The company sells across 18 divisions and 23 market segments with no common physical unit, which is a legitimate reason not to publish a blended realisation; but the consequence for an analyst is that price and volume cannot be separated, and management has twice declined to separate them when asked directly. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026; CALL May 2026)

Because volume is not disclosed, the statement 'order growth of 50% is mostly volume' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) cannot be verified, and neither can the counter-hypothesis put by a UBS analyst that 'bulk of this is value growth in pricing'. [F] (CALL Aug 2026) Both are unfalsifiable on the public record. That is itself a disclosure finding.

subsections.title: What would have to be true for unit economics to improve

items: Copper, silver and aluminium prices flatten and the rupee stops depreciating, so that the two published price increases are not overtaken before they take effect. Management's own research says the opposite is more likely over the next few quarters. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

The Quality Control Order certification pipeline completes so locally made, locally sourced product replaces imported certified material. This recovers a quantified 0.75-0.8 pp in Electrification. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025)

Revenue mix shifts back towards services and Process Automation, where forex clauses and installed-base pricing protect margin. Currently the mix is moving the other way: services were 12% of Q1 CY2026 revenue and Automation's backlog is shrinking. [F] (PPT May 2026; AR2025 p.153)

Utilisation rises enough for the 0.18 pp per 1% scale factor to outrun input costs - which requires roughly 17% incremental revenue to offset the 3.0 pp of material cost seen in the last bridge. [E] (CALL Aug 2026)

Royalty, trademark and group service charges grow no faster than revenue. They grew 17.7% against 8.3% revenue growth in CY2025. [E] (AR2025 p.333, p.334, p.288) This is the one lever entirely outside minority shareholders' influence.

Competition intensity abates. Management has flagged Japanese, Korean and Chinese entrants and European competitors adding Indian capacity, and expects to 'continue to see the expansion of the competitors' as the market grows. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [AI] This one is unlikely to reverse.

blocks.text: **Our statements data is incomplete and readers should know exactly how.** The annual series contains only four columns - Dec 2011, Dec 2012, Dec 2024 and Dec 2025 - not the usual ten years. [F] (NUMBERS) There is a twelve-year gap between the second and third columns. The quarterly series contains twelve non-contiguous quarters: Jun 2019, Sep 2019, Mar 2022, Jun 2022, then Sep 2024 through Jun 2026 consecutively. [F] (NUMBERS) Return on capital employed is null for CY2011 and CY2024; return on equity is null for CY2011; five-year cumulative cash conversion and five-year free cash flow are both null. [F] (NUMBERS) Wherever a longer series matters we have used the annual report's own five-year summary for CY2021-CY2025, which is on a different basis. [F] (AR2025 p.27) No trend statement in this report should be read as a ten-year trend.

items: **Other income is almost entirely interest on the cash pile.** Other income was Rs 352.36 cr in CY2025 and Rs 353.40 cr in CY2024; interest income within the cash flow adjustment was Rs 348.51 cr and Rs 343.29 cr. [F] (AR2025 p.288, p.289) That is 15.8% of CY2025 profit before tax from treasury, not operations. [E] Our statements data puts other income at 15.7% of PBT for CY2025 and 13.7% for CY2024. [F] (NUMBERS)

**Trailing twelve-month earnings are not comparable to anything.** TTM other income is Rs 1,799 cr against Rs 349 cr in CY2025; TTM PBT Rs 3,508 cr; TTM PAT Rs 2,988 cr; TTM EPS Rs 141. [F] (NUMBERS) The Mar 2026 quarter alone carried Rs 1,541 cr of other income at a 6% effective tax rate - the Robotics slump sale at not less than Rs 1,568.20 cr. [F] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.341) Any multiple computed on TTM earnings is therefore understated relative to recurring earnings. [AI]

**Employee cost grew more than twice as fast as revenue.** Rs 974.81 cr against Rs 821.93 cr, up 18.6% on 8.3% revenue growth, including a Rs 65 cr New Labour Code charge that management deliberately took through normal expenses rather than as an exceptional item. [F] (AR2025 p.288); [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [E] We regard that classification choice as conservative and appropriate.

**Inside 'other expenses', group charges are the growth line.** Total other expenses rose 8.1% to Rs 2,130.54 cr, but information technology expenses rose 31.8% to Rs 352.21 cr, services from third parties 37.6% to Rs 211.40 cr, group management fees 14.4% to Rs 245.30 cr, royalty and technology fees 12.6% to Rs 430.92 cr and trade-mark fees 7.3% to Rs 128.78 cr. [F] (AR2025 p.316) [E]

**Two provision lines released, materially helping CY2025.** Warranty (net) fell from Rs 80.24 cr to Rs 11.97 cr and loss allowance swung from a Rs 41.11 cr charge to an Rs 8.43 cr credit - Rs 117.8 cr of combined relief, about 0.9 pp of margin. [E] (AR2025 p.316) Exchange rate difference also swung from a Rs 27.87 cr loss to a Rs 23.69 cr gain. [F] (AR2025 p.316) Against this, inventory obsolescence went from a Rs 1.17 cr reversal to a Rs 19.79 cr charge. [F] (AR2025 p.308)
**Finance cost is lease interest, not debt.** Rs 19.89 cr against nil borrowings; interest cover 112.5x in CY2025 and 157.9x in CY2024. [F] (AR2025 p.288, p.27; NUMBERS)
**Tax is unremarkable.** Effective tax 25.1-25.5% in CY2024 and CY2025; current tax Rs 521.62 cr and deferred Rs 38.92 cr in CY2025. [F] (AR2025 p.288); [F] (NUMBERS)

**Liquidated damages are rising.** Deductions from gross revenue for liquidated damages went from Rs 26.59 cr to Rs 42.42 cr while total variable consideration stayed flat at about Rs 120 cr. [F] (AR2025 p.338) [AI] A 60% increase in penalties for late or non-conforming delivery is a small but real execution signal.

**Nearly 43% of the balance sheet is cash.** Cash and cash equivalents Rs 1,552.57 cr plus other bank balances Rs 4,282.30 cr equals Rs 5,834.87 cr of Rs 13,638.48 cr total assets, or 74.5% of equity. [E] (AR2025 p.287) Deposits with maturity over three months fell from Rs 4,566.87 cr to Rs 4,275.20 cr while short-dated deposits rose from Rs 640.40 cr to Rs 1,240.00 cr - a shortening of treasury duration, consistent with preparing for a large outflow. [F] (AR2025 p.307, p.308) [AI]
**Non-current tax assets rose 36.5% to Rs 250.64 cr** from Rs 183.62 cr. [F] (AR2025 p.287) [E] Refunds are accumulating slowly; there is no explanation in the extracted disclosure.

**Current other financial assets tripled** from Rs 95.75 cr to Rs 302.15 cr. [F] (AR2025 p.287) The cash-flow statement shows a Rs 143.11 cr mark-to-market gain on forward and commodity contracts reversed out of operating cash flow, which plausibly accounts for most of the increase. [F] (AR2025 p.289) [AI] The company does not reconcile the two.

**Receivables quality is mixed.** Gross trade receivables Rs 3,404.70 cr, of which credit-impaired Rs 131.84 cr fully provided, plus Rs 96.53 cr of expected credit loss allowance on the rest, up from Rs 80.74 cr. [F] (AR2025 p.307) Receivables considered good but over one year old rose from Rs 131.04 cr to Rs 179.52 cr, an increase of 37%. [E] (AR2025 p.307) Recoverability of trade receivables is one of the two key audit matters. [F] (AR2025 p.280)

**Inventory rose 15.5% on 8.3% revenue growth**, to Rs 2,052.98 cr, driven by raw materials and components (Rs 1,144.58 cr to Rs 1,288.45 cr) and stock-in-trade (Rs 104.69 cr to Rs 205.53 cr, nearly doubling). [F] (AR2025 p.308) [E] Management attributes this to deliberate Quality Control Order stocking. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025)

**Contract balances.** Advances from customers Rs 468.39 cr, billing in excess of contract revenue Rs 618.86 cr, contract assets Rs 173.65 cr. [F] (AR2025 p.334) Contract assets rose 23.9% - unbilled revenue growing faster than sales. [E]

**Equity.** Rs 7,835.99 cr, up from Rs 7,075.40 cr; share capital unchanged at Rs 42.38 cr on 21,19,08,375 shares of Rs 2. [F] (AR2025 p.287, p.309) No dilution. ESOP outstanding at December 2025 was 33,644 units at a weighted average of 1.20 - immaterial. [F] (AR2025 p.323)

subsections.title: CARO, audit trail and books of account

items: **CARO: clean for the holding company, unavailable for the subsidiary.** The auditors report 'we have not reported any qualifications or adverse remarks' for ABB India Limited. For ABB Robotics India Private Limited, whose audit under Section 143 had not been completed, 'the CARO report as applicable in respect of this subsidiary company is not available'. [F] (AR2025 p.282) Given the subsidiary had Rs 1,00,000 of assets and nil turnover, this is immaterial. [F] (AR2025 p.106) [AI]

**There is a modification on the maintenance of books of account.** The auditors report that proper books have been kept 'except (a) that the back-up of audit trail of database layer of the accounting software used by the Holding Company for transactions related to receipts and payments is not maintained on server physically located in India until 11 December 2025 and (b) for matters stated in the paragraph 2B(f) below'. [F] (AR2025 p.283) This is a qualification of the Section 143(3)(b) statement, not of the opinion.

**Three Rule 11(g) audit-trail exceptions are reported:** the auditors are unable to comment whether audit trail was enabled up to 10 December 2025 at the database layer of third-party-operated software used for initiating and approving journal entries; unable to comment on enablement up to 12 July 2025 for customer and vendor master data; and unable to comment for employee master data from 23 June 2025, in each case in the absence of an independent auditor's report on the third-party service provider's controls. [F] (AR2025 p.284)

**One of these is still not compliant.** The company's own Note 47 states that for employee master data maintained by a third-party provider, the audit trail facility 'is not compliant with the statutory requirements. The management is currently evaluating the implementation of formal measures to comply'. Customer/vendor master data became compliant from 13 July 2025 and journal-entry initiation from 11 December 2025. [F] (AR2025 p.340)
**No tampering was found** where the audit trail was enabled, and preserved trails have been retained per statutory retention requirements. [F] (AR2025 p.284)

blocks.text: Audit-trail non-compliance is common in Indian filings and is not evidence of misstatement. But three separate exceptions, one of which remained uncured at the reporting date and is being 'evaluated' rather than fixed, in a company with 75% foreign parent ownership and Rs 3,179 cr of related-party purchases, is a control finding that deserves a direct question to the audit committee. [F] (AR2025 p.284, p.340, p.333) [AI]

items: **No restatements** are disclosed. Prior-year figures in the cash flow statement were 'regrouped/reclassified, where necessary' - standard language. [F] (AR2025 p.289) Equity share capital shows no changes due to prior-period errors. [F] (AR2025 p.290)

**Conservative classification of the Labour Code charge.** Rs 65 cr was taken through normal personnel expenses rather than as an exceptional item because management 'believe[s] that it is better to be conservative than taking an item to show a better profitability per se'. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [AI] We agree with the choice; it is a mark in favour of the accounting culture.
**No exceptional items in CY2025 or CY2024.** Profit before tax before and after exceptional items are identical in both years; CY2022 and CY2021 did carry exceptional items. [F] (AR2025 p.27)

**Provision releases were material and should be watched.** Warranty (net) at Rs 11.97 cr against Rs 80.24 cr, and a loss-allowance credit of Rs 8.43 cr against a Rs 41.11 cr charge, together worth Rs 117.8 cr. [E] (AR2025 p.316) The warranty provision balance itself barely moved (Rs 293.43 cr to Rs 287.32 cr), so this is a lower charge rather than a release of the balance - less aggressive than it first appears, but still a tailwind that reversed no reserve. [F] (AR2025 p.312) [AI]

**Common control and unusual accounting:** the only such transaction is the Robotics carve-out, and it was handled with visible process - independent valuations by Ernst & Young Merchant Banking Services LLP and Bansi S. Mehta & Co., a fairness opinion from ICICI Securities, and shareholder approval required. [F] (AR2025 p.100) [AI] That is a stronger governance wrapper than most Indian related-party asset transfers receive.

**Revenue recognition split** is disclosed: Rs 11,119.32 cr at a point in time and Rs 1,946.20 cr over time in CY2025. [F] (AR2025 p.334) The over-time portion - the part subject to percentage-of-completion judgement and the first key audit matter - is only 14.7% of revenue. [E] That materially limits the scope for revenue-recognition manipulation. [AI]

**Related-party terms are asserted, not evidenced.** 'The sales to and purchases from related parties are made on terms equivalent to those that prevail in arm's length transactions.' [F] (AR2025 p.337) No transfer-pricing benchmarking study, no comparable-uncontrolled-price analysis and no royalty-rate justification appear in the extracted disclosure.

blocks.text: **Overall accounting-quality assessment: good, with a control gap and a transparency gap.** Unmodified opinion, clean CARO, clean secretarial audit, no exceptional items, no restatements, minimal intangibles, conservative treatment of the Labour Code charge, and an independently valued related-party carve-out. [F] (AR2025 p.279, p.282, p.116, p.27, p.100) The two blemishes are the uncured employee-master-data audit trail and the absence of any transfer-pricing evidence behind Rs 4,593 cr of gross annual payments to the group. [F] (AR2025 p.340); [E] (AR2025 p.333, p.334)

**What the documents did not cover.** No forensic or special audit is mentioned. No whistleblower complaint statistics appear in the extracted text. No auditor rotation history or tenure is disclosed in the extracted text. No details of income-tax assessment years under dispute beyond the Rs 10.30 cr aggregate. No internal financial controls adverse findings. No management letter points. No disclosure of transfer-pricing assessments or advance pricing agreements. Each of these is a gap in our evidence, not a clean bill of health. [F]

subsections.title: Interpreting the DCF and its assumptions

blocks.text: The DCF says the operating business is worth Rs 814.8 per share in the base case, Rs 452.9 in the bear case and Rs 1,134.6 in the bull case, against a book value of Rs 441 and a price of Rs 7,270. [F] (NUMBERS) Three observations follow.

items: **The model is internally consistent and moderately conservative on operations.** It uses a starting growth rate drawn from the company's own median record, a flat margin at the CY2025 level rather than the depressed current run rate, a capex rule marginally stricter than actual capital intensity, and a working-capital absorption of 15.7 days against an actual cash conversion cycle of 21 days. [F] (NUMBERS) None of those is aggressive against the company. [AI]

**Its two most contestable inputs are the discount rate and the cash treatment.** A 15% WACC for a AAA, net-cash, 22% return-on-equity industrial with a global parent is high; and the equity bridge deducts Rs 85 crore of lease liabilities while ignoring Rs 5,835-7,200 crore of treasury assets. [F] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.287) [AI] Both push the output down. The sensitivity grid bounds the first at Rs 1,072.5 in the most generous corner; the second is worth roughly Rs 275-340 per share of assets. [F] (NUMBERS); [E]

**Neither correction, nor both together, closes a gap of this size.** Base value Rs 814.8 against a price of Rs 7,270 is a factor of about 8.9x. [E] (NUMBERS) [AI] The honest statement is not that the DCF has found mispricing of a modest kind; it is that a discounted-cash-flow framework applied to this company's disclosed cash flows produces an answer in a completely different order of magnitude from the market price, and an investor must decide which they believe describes reality.

The single most important finding in this report is that the gap between price and evidenced cash flows is not a matter of degree. It is not closed by a lower discount rate (the sensitivity grid tops out at Rs 1,072.5), by adding back the cash (roughly Rs 275-340 per share), by assuming a full margin recovery (the bull case at 17% is still below CY2024's 19% and still values the equity at Rs 1,134.6), or by any combination of the three. blocks.text: We owe the other side of this a serious hearing, because a nine-times discrepancy between a model and a liquid, widely covered large-cap usually means the model is measuring the wrong thing rather than that the market has lost its mind for years. Four points deserve weight.

items: **A 15% WACC with a 5.5% terminal growth rate implies a terminal exit of roughly 11.7x year-five free cash flow.** [E] (NUMBERS) For a franchise with a CRISIL AAA rating, an A/Stable-rated parent, no external debt for eight years, a 22% return on equity, 0.1% soft assets and a 50-year installed base in Indian industry, that terminal treatment is severe. [F] (RATING; NUMBERS; AR2025 p.287) A DCF calibrated to this company's actual risk would produce a higher number - though the grid shows how much higher, and it is not enough.

**The model gives no credit to the balance sheet.** Rs 5,835-7,200 crore of cash, Rs 348 crore a year of interest income excluded from an EBITDA-based FCFF model, and Rs 4,000 crore that CRISIL says is earmarked for organic and inorganic growth. [F] (AR2025 p.287, p.289; RATING); [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) An operating-cash-flow model systematically undervalues a company that is 43% treasury. [AI]

**Scarcity has a price.** ABB India is one of a very small number of ways for Indian institutional capital to own a AAA-rated, promoter-backed, debt-free multinational industrial franchise with direct exposure to electrification, automation and data centres. Domestic institutions have raised their holding from 5.42% to 9.89% in eight quarters while foreign institutions sold. [F] (NUMBERS) [AI] A DCF cannot price a supply constraint in investable assets; that is a real economic phenomenon even if it is not a cash flow.

**The operating business is genuinely inflecting.** Orders up 50% in the latest quarter, backlog at a record Rs 11,900 crore, book-to-bill of 1.28x in the half year, a sixth manufacturing location, and data centres at 15-17% of quarterly order intake. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); [E] An investor buying a ten-year compounding story is not underwriting the next five years of free cash flow; they are underwriting the terminal franchise. [AI]

blocks.text: **Where the counter-argument stops.** Every one of those four points is legitimate and every one of them is bounded. Adjust the WACC to its most generous tested level and add the entire cash balance and take the bull operating case, and the model still produces a number far below the market. The counter-argument therefore cannot be that the DCF is wrong by a factor of two; it has to be that the DCF is the wrong lens entirely and the stock is priced on scarcity, index inclusion and terminal-franchise belief rather than on discounted cash flows. That is a coherent position. It is also, by construction, a position with no valuation floor - which is exactly what an investor should know before taking it. [AI]

subsections.title: Where the price sits, and what drives the gap

blocks.text: At Rs 7,270 the share trades 84.4% above the most optimistic fair value our DCF model produces and 88.8% above its base case, with a book value of Rs 441 and a price/book of 16.49x. [F] (NUMBERS) The reverse DCF resolves what that means in operating terms: today's enterprise value requires about 81.7% annual sales growth for five years, against a base-case equivalent of 10.8%, a five-year actual record of 17.4% and a best-ever year of 21.9%. [F] (NUMBERS); [E] (AR2025 p.27) We issue no rating and no price target, and we have produced no valuation figure of our own.

**What drives the gap, honestly assessed.** Three things, in descending order of size. First and largest: the market is not valuing this company on discounted cash flows at all. It is valuing a scarce, AAA-rated, promoter-backed, debt-free vehicle for Indian electrification and data-centre exposure, and scarcity value has no DCF representation. Domestic institutions have raised their stake from 5.42% to 9.89% in eight quarters while foreign institutions cut theirs from 12.28% to 7.67%. [F] (NUMBERS) [AI] Second: the model's discount rate is severe for this credit - a 15% WACC and 5.5% terminal growth for a company with nil external debt, Rs 7,200 crore of net cash and a AAA rating, with the entire 13.5% WACC row of the sensitivity grid topping out at Rs 1,072.5. [F] (NUMBERS; RATING) Third: the model gives the balance sheet no credit at all, ignoring roughly Rs 275-340 per share of treasury assets and the Rs 348 crore a year of interest income they produce. [E] (AR2025 p.287, p.289)

Taking all three corrections at their most generous - the lowest tested discount rate, the highest tested terminal growth, the bull operating case, and the whole cash balance added back - does not bring the model within a factor of five of the price. [E] (NUMBERS) The conclusion an investor must reach is therefore binary rather than incremental: either discounted cash flow is the wrong lens for this asset, or the price embeds expectations that four earnings calls, a 350-page annual report and a AAA rating rationale do not support. Both positions are intellectually coherent. Only one of them has a floor.

Process Automation demonstrates a real installed-base moat: it held a 16.4% segment PBIT margin through the worst input-cost year in a decade because it has no Quality Control Order exposure, carries forex variation clauses in long-term contracts and derives about 30% of revenue from services. [F] (AR2025 p.330); [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; CALL Aug 2026)

Operating leverage is real and quantified by management: a 2.1 percentage-point scale benefit on an 11.8% sequential revenue increase, roughly 0.18 points of EBITDA margin per 1% of revenue, against a stated capacity headroom target of 15-20%. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); [E] (NUMBERS)
bear_points: The price requires arithmetic the company has never produced: the reverse DCF implies about 81.7% annual sales growth for five years against a base-case equivalent of 10.8%, a five-year actual CAGR of 17.4% and a best-ever year of 21.9%. Bear, base and bull fair values are Rs 452.9, Rs 814.8 and Rs 1,134.6 against a price of Rs 7,270, and the most generous cell of the entire WACC and terminal-growth sensitivity grid is Rs 1,072.5. [E] (NUMBERS); [E] (AR2025 p.27)

Margin compression is six quarters old and majority structural on management's own decomposition: operating margin fell from 20% (Dec 2024) to 13% (Jun 2026), with 1-1.5 points of permanently lost post-COVID price premium, about 1 point of competition intensity, a Rs 65 cr Labour Code step-up and a structurally short-rupee position of Rs 6,765 cr of foreign exchange used against Rs 1,568 cr earned. The CFO explicitly declined to commit to mid-teen EBITDA margins. [F] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.109); [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; CALL May 2026; CALL Aug 2026)

The record CY2025 order headline was carried by the segment that has been sold: company orders rose 8% to Rs 14,115 cr, but Robotics orders went from Rs 534 cr to Rs 1,217 cr on a one-time automotive order while Electrification orders actually fell from Rs 6,068 cr to Rs 5,878 cr. Ex-Robotics, orders grew about 3.0%. [F] (AR2025 p.28, p.155, p.150); [E]

A majority of profit before tax is paid to the parent group with no disclosed benchmarking: royalty, trademark, IT and group management charges of Rs 1,387.87 cr equal 62% of consolidated PBT and grew 17.7% in a year when PBT fell 11.3%; related-party purchases rose from 34.22% to 39.46% of total purchases; the only assurance is a boilerplate arm's-length assertion, and there is no non-compete or order-allocation policy. [E] (AR2025 p.333, p.334, p.288); [F] (AR2025 p.174, p.337)

The parent is capturing Indian demand the listed entity cannot serve: ABB Group reported 81-82% order growth against ABB India's 50%, with Indian customers placing marine and port system orders directly on European ABB units because ABB India lacks 'the system in this particular country at this point of time or the competency'. Promoter holding is pinned at the 75.00% statutory ceiling, so any change can only be downward, and FII holding has fallen from 12.28% to 7.67% over eight quarters. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); [F] (NUMBERS)
watch_points: Backlog conversion at the 13 November 2026 results: management committed that at least 40% of the Rs 11,900 cr backlog - about Rs 4,760 cr - converts to revenue across Q3 and Q4 CY2026, and that there is 'no slow moving or a non-moving order'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); [E]; [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS)

Material cost as a share of revenue, the cleanest read on whether the two published price increases are landing: about 63% in Q2 CY2026 against 61.3% in Q1 CY2026, 60.2% for CY2025 and 57.6% in Q1 CY2025. A move back below 60% would be the first genuine evidence of pass-through. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); [F] (PPT May 2026)

Whether order growth holds once channel stocking normalises: management confirmed partners 'are very excited to place a stock order' and the Managing Director attributed the 50% growth to market normalisation after a lull rather than to share gain. Growth below 10% year on year would confirm the restocking read. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Automation backlog, the quality signal in the order book: Rs 2,397 cr (Dec 2024) to Rs 2,255 cr (Dec 2025) to Rs 2,147 cr (Mar 2026). A fall below Rs 2,100 cr would confirm structural decline in the highest-margin, most defensible segment. [F] (AR2025 p.153; PPT May 2026)

The CFO appointment, said on 31 July 2026 to be about two months from completion, ahead of T. K. Sridhar becoming Managing Director on 1 January 2027 - the entire finance and executive leadership turning over at once. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)
guidance: Backlog conversion: 'over the INR11,900 crores, whatever we have, we will consume at least 40% in the next 2 quarters' revenues what we need to have. Plus, we will have some left for that one bill to meet the revenue commitments with the customers. And the balance will go to the next 4 quarters of 2027.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Backlog quality: 'Backlog, strong backlog, INR11,900 crores of order backlog, in which there is no slow moving or a non-moving order. Everything you will get materialized over a period of time as scheduled with the customers.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

EBITDA margin - explicitly refused: 'today, I'm not comfortable to tell that what is that mid-teens of EBITDA margins, which we will do. Most important is protect what we are today so that we are able to develop the revenues and the orders in a good manner and then start to grow from there. That's what we are looking at it on a short-term basis.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Margin recovery conditions: margin improvement is 'all dependent on 3 things... will the material cost, the metal prices and the forex rates remain at today's level... And we see that the mix, and we don't have any distortion in terms of supply chain... Probably we get better leverage of the operating leverage going forward in the next 2 quarters. But our research says... we will still have certain headwinds from that particular side.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)
Input cost outlook: 'elevated commodity prices and continued rupee depreciation will be extended as what our research says. I think we are preparing as to how to manage this.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Pricing: two publicly available price lists have been issued; 'this is really supporting us in terms of trying to compensate the EBIT'; but 'there will always be a lag. If the prices stabilize, the input prices stabilize, then you will have this particular lag catching up. But otherwise, this still will continue.' Quantum not disclosed. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Capacity policy: 'we want to make sure that we have at least 15% of our headroom to cater for the future demand. So that means at every, any moment of time, our capacity utilisation hovers between, say, 80% to 85% or 90% is the maximum... this capex, what we are doing at this point of time and every year will help us maintain that momentum of 15% to 20% headroom of increase in sales.' Capex referenced as 'this USD75 million, USD80 million capex'; the ABB India Limited share is not stated. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Data-centre capacity investment: 'we are investing quite heavily in increasing our capacity, because we are definitely seeing that picking up which will come - the demand will multifold in the coming quarters and maybe like 2027, 2028, we will be struggling to meet those demand.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Quality Control Order: 'I will not say it is completely behind, but it is definitely relaxed and we got an extension of time, and we also learned how to meet those type of requirements' (Distribution Solutions); 'QCO is not behind us, but at the same time, I think it's supporting our business growth as well' (Electrification Products). This follows a November 2025 guide of resolution 'in another three to four quarters'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026; CALL Nov 2025)

Order mix by segment, Q2 CY2026: 'Data Centers orders in this quarter has been almost 15% to 17% of our orders came from base orders. Metals and Mining was 15% and then oil and gas was 9% and Buildings and Infra was 8%. Renewables was 6%.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)
Order classification change: 'we want to move away from differentiating between base orders and large orders... in this quarter is everything is base orders.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Group versus listed-entity order gap: the difference between the group's 82% order growth and ABB India's 50% reflected Rs 124 cr of orders placed by Indian customers on other ABB companies, described as 'just a onetime what you see', arising from a novated contract and from marine and ports systems 'where we don't have the system in this particular country at this point of time or the competency'. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Railways and metro: 'we have long-term contracts with the railway exposure, and those are not difficult... the predictability of revenues is there in front of us and also the price predictability is also there for us, including the service that we will deliver to them alongside the delivery. So we don't see any specific pressure at this point of time.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Market share: declined to claim any. 'The market digested whatever the previous year's growth was, and now it's normalizing again. So I would say these growth rates that we see, it comes in a spurt after the lull in the market and then they normalize to a kind of a level that we like.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)
Water and wastewater market: 'the ABB play in this is 4% to 8 percentage. And the midterm growth, which if you look at is roughly about 10% CAGR over the next 5 years to come.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Dividend: interim dividend of Rs 90 per share, 'which includes the proceeds which we got from the divestment of robotics plus a 50% payout ratio of what we do from the normal earnings per share.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Leadership: T. K. Sridhar accorded Managing Director Designate status by the board in May 2026, effective 1 January 2027; 'the CFO search is on, we should be complete in the next couple of months, and then we have the process of induction there as well.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Rotork acquisition by the parent: 'it is pretty early for us to comment... the shareholders of Rotork have still not approved this particular deal... we have nothing to comment at this point of time.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Volume versus price split of the 50% order growth: 'we normally don't look at it from that volume and price led because it's all embedded in the offerings what we do... it will be mostly volume, right, because price, of course, has a lag.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

Macro outlook for the next two to three quarters: 'government capex which is expected to pick up, the private consumption which is going to drive, and a robust manufacturing base what we have and start dealing with geopolitical uncertainty as well as current situation and the subnormal monsoon.' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)
